geometry.name: rib200

provenance_by_field.film_nm: printed (SMTAI render, conflicts with GF 160 nm; 07 D21)
provenance_by_field.note: GF 45SPCLO photonics SOI 160 nm and BOX 2 um are printed (GF-IMAPS, 01 section 4.2); the partial-etch (slab) depth, the rib width of Lightmatter's MRM and the sidewall angle are NOT public. Width 400 nm: Lightmatter SMTAI render (400 x 200 nm, printed for an unspecified product) and the BU 45CLO rib ring (w = 410 nm, R = 8 um, printed, Al Qubaisi et al. CLEO 2021). Slab: assumed, 60 nm on 160 and 80 nm on 200 (slab/film 0.375-0.4, typical foundry ribs such as 220/90 and 220/70 nm; the same values as junction.py), swept for the Jacobian and in slab_sweep.

geometry.provenance_note: one provenance word for the whole cross-section (the weakest of its parts): every hypothesis has at least one unpublished dimension (slab depth, rib width, sidewall angle or cladding), so it is 'assumed'; per-field provenance is in provenance_by_field

ranges_not_assigned.sidewall_deg: 90 deg (assumed); no range assigned and no sensitivity computed; realize has no sidewall dimension
ranges_not_assigned.clad: SiO2 (beol) above and beside the core, SiO2 (thermal) BOX, indices from mrm.materials: the cladding stack (no liner, no index spread, thickness) is assumed and has no range

materials.si_index_model: li1980 temperature shape on the frey level

inputs.r_ref_rule: self-consistent with fsr_design_thz: c / (2 pi r_ref n_g,bent(r_ref)) = FSR

memory.cap: tools/memguard.py --limit-gb 3 --heavy (the former per-job cap; the heavy default is now 6 GB)
memory.reduced_because: the first design was coarsened before the first full run, right after a 5-solve probe at mesh scale 1.0 (rib160, closed and PML windows up to 128k dofs) peaked at 2.61 GB under the 3 GB cap; the transcript does not state the reason, and run time (about 3x per solve) was a second factor. The finest level (7.07 nm, ~2x the elements of 10 nm) could not run under 3 GB.
memory.accuracy_cost: the reported values carry the production-mesh bias of validation.production_mesh_bias instead of the ~3x smaller bias of the 10 nm level

estimate.model: empirical RSS model of the first run's probes: RSS ~ 0.18 GB + 6.25 kB per dof of every live FEM problem (fit to the per-scale maxrss of a convergence probe, 10-39k dofs per problem, 0.24-1.17 GB; it predicts 2.70 GB for the scale-1.0 probe with four live problems, 403k dofs, measured 2.61 GB). A long production run adds an overhead (allocator growth, Tidy3D at 2.5 nm) taken from its measured peak; uncertainty ~30 %

crosscheck_tidy3d_uncertainty.note: delta = FEM - Tidy3D limit; the FEM matches Tidy3D within the Tidy3D extrapolation uncertainty (order sensitivity; |finest - f0| is the conservative bound in the FEM's discretization_error convention), not to |delta|. The bend shift is the sharper cross-check.

production_mesh_bias.note: bias = f(production mesh) - f0 for the values reported in the data file; discretization_error there is |f(finest) - f0|. lambda_res_bias_nm = lambda0 * bias(n_eff_bent) / n_g at fixed r_ref.

assumptions.substrate: omitted: the 2 um BOX makes substrate leakage negligible (decay exp(-2 k0 sqrt(n_eff^2 - n_ox^2) * 2 um) < 1e-14)
assumptions.expansion: ring length follows the substrate-clamped Si alpha_L; the change of the cross-section (width, film) with temperature and stress-optic terms are neglected (< 0.5 % of dn_eff/dT, estimated from the Jacobian x alpha_Si x dimensions)
assumptions.doping: undoped Si; the junction's free-carrier index change is in junction_<xsec>.json

geometry.film_nm: printed (SMTAI render, conflicts with GF 160 nm; 07 D21)
